name: Ocean View Diner
rationale: Chrome counter and big harbor-facing windows read exactly like the script's dawn diner, and the vinyl booths are period-right.
flags: confirm pre-opening access for a dawn call

name: Chrome & Vinyl Diner
address: 200 N Pacific Coast Hwy, Redondo Beach, CA
rationale: Strong retro interior, but the ocean sits across a parking lot, so the window sightline needs a long lens.
flags: ocean not directly visible from booths

name: Santa Monica Pier Pancakes
address: 330 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA
rationale: Great pier light and ocean backdrop, but the room is bright and touristy rather than melancholy.

name: Malibu Seaside Cafe
rationale: Beautiful ocean frontage, but it reads modern-coastal, so heavy set dressing would be needed for the noir tone.

name: Point Vicente Lighthouse
address: 31550 Palos Verdes Dr W, Rancho Palos Verdes, CA
rationale: Whitewashed tower on a true cliff with surf below; the dusk light wraps the headland just as scripted.

name: Point Fermin Lighthouse
address: 807 W Paseo Del Mar, San Pedro, CA
rationale: Clifftop Victorian lighthouse in a park; charming and accessible, but more manicured than windswept.

name: Marina del Rey Breakwater Light
rationale: A working light, but it sits on a flat jetty with no cliff and no crashing surf.

name: Werdin Place
rationale: A genuine narrow brick alley off Broadway with iron fire escapes; a longtime film alley that needs little dressing.

name: Broadway Theater District Alley
rationale: Marquee neon spill plus a wet-down would reflect beautifully; brick walls and iron are all there.

name: Arts District Service Alley
rationale: Industrial brick and loading docks; grittier and easier to lock off, but there is no theater marquee nearby.
